brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 in exchange for a 6% price cut — their cash is stuck for 101 days, so early payment is worth about 12% a year to them.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 6% price cut if we pay in 15 days instead of 30.
priceAsk.target: A 6% reduction (roughly half their 12.16% borrowing rate, matched to the 15-day acceleration).
priceAsk.basis: Their cash is stuck for 101 days vs 64 days at similar firms, and they borrow money at 12.16% — so paying them 15 days earlier frees up cash worth about that rate to them. Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band (₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg), so a 6% cut still leaves them profitable while rewarding us for faster payment.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (instead of the current 30 days) in exchange for the 6% price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹26.60 L in cash that we tie up earlier, but we recover it through the price cut — and we help them close their 101-day cash gap.

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, so there's little room for a hard price squeeze on its own. But their cash is stuck for 101 days (way longer than the 64 days at similar firms), and they borrow at 12.16% — so early payment is very valuable to them. They owe 1.25 times their own cash (₹282.62 Cr in total debt) and their rating is middling (CARE BBB+ / Stable), with EPF payment delays flagged. We're only 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we're small to them — but cash is tight, and a 15-day payment deal solves a real problem for them while earning us a discount.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than peers
They borrow money at a high rate
They keep very little profit per sale
They owe a lot relative to their own cash
Our spend is small to them
Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band
evidence.figure: ₹205–305/kg typical ₹250/kg — verdict: MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — a proven second source for laminate sachets, revenue ₹2611.64 Cr.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — can handle laminate volume at scale, revenue ₹16492.00 Cr.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, specialises in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second source, revenue ₹222.04 Cr.

risks: Their rating is middling (CARE BBB+ / Stable) and they have EPF payment delays — watch supply reliability and don't push so hard that you tip a supplier already in the grey zone (Altman Z 2.36).
They cover their interest only 1.94 times — a tight margin that means big volume swings or payment squeezes could strain them.
We're small (0.61% of their revenue), so we have limited volume leverage — lead with the payment-for-price swap, not threats to walk.
If we move payment to 15 days, we tie up ₹26.60 L more cash — make sure the 6% saving pays back that working-capital cost.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help you close your cash cycle — if we pay you in 15 days instead of 30, can you pass on half the financing saving as a 6% price reduction?
